answer: The umber counter is kept in grove and fable publishes each reset. A bond is refunded only after 29 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. A hostile operator therefore has to keep every alias continuously active for 29 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 29 times over for the same share of the pool. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
